common_driver_discrepancy.question: Why does the current recomputation (41.6454%) differ from the retained measurement (40.0284%)?
common_driver_discrepancy.answer: It is NOT configuration drift. The retained due-diligence package's own 11 itemized effective weights sum to exactly 41.6454% — identical to the current recomputation to four decimal places. Every fund allocation in that table (SPY 15%, VEA 7%, VWO 1%) still matches targets.yaml, and the retained NVDA effective weight (7.149%) reproduces exactly. The discrepancy is therefore INTERNAL to the retained evidence: its headline 40.0284% figure is inconsistent with its own line items in the same file.
common_driver_discrepancy.arithmetic_reconciliation: An exhaustive search of all 2,047 non-empty subsets found exactly ONE combination reproducing the headline: total effective (41.6454%) minus the ETF-embedded components of LLY, TSLA and AAPL (1.6170pp) = 40.0284%. The exclusion is unique at 1e-9 tolerance.
common_driver_discrepancy.corroboration: The package's separate effective_mega6_weight (0.29999) IS exactly reproducible from the same line items (NVDA+MSFT+AMZN+GOOGL+AVGO+META), which supports the line items being the reliable part of the retained package.
common_driver_discrepancy.intent: UNRESOLVED — the retained package documents no inclusion rule, describes the figure as an 'estimate', and gives no reason why LLY, TSLA and AAPL would contribute direct weight but not embedded weight. This artifact establishes the arithmetic, not the intent.
common_driver_discrepancy.consequence: Whether the canonical target portfolio breaches the 40% common-driver ceiling depends on which inclusion rule is authoritative, and no accepted decision states one.
